candidates.attacker_control: The XML document being parsed is attacker-influenceable in normal client-library use: a remote SPARQL endpoint (or a MITM on plain HTTP) controls the response Content-Type and body that SPARQLProtocolSession feeds to QueryResultIO.createTupleParser(); RDF4J's federation path lets an attacker-chosen SERVICE URI become an in-process SPARQLRepository (SPARQLServiceResolver.createService -> SPARQLFederatedService -> SPARQLRepository), so a SERIAL SERVICE endpoint's response is parsed by the same client code and entity-expanded values are streamed back into the outer query result. Any application that parses untrusted/stored SPARQL XML tuple results is exposed as well.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that the boolean path in the same class (lines 87-163) and XMLReaderBasedParser/RDFXMLParser/TriXParser do apply the same compulsory features, confirming intent; XMLParserSettings defaults DISALLOW_DOCTYPE_DECL/EXTERNAL_GENERAL_ENTITIES/EXTERNAL_PARAMETER_ENTITIES to secure values but they are never applied on the tuple path. Verified no other code hardens XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader() and no global JAXP property is set anywhere in the snapshot. Noted the possible external mitigation that a JVM could be launched with restricted javax.xml.accessExternalDTD/accessExternalSchema (not present here; default JAXP behavior permits external entity resolution). I did not execute code or construct a payload, so exploitability rests on standard JAXP/Java 8 default behavior.
candidates.impact: XML External Entity processing on the parsing process: (a) local file disclosure - file content can be inserted into result literals that the caller/attacker receives (non-blind when the caller is a remote client querying a federated RDF4J server, blind/out-of-band otherwise); (b) SSRF/port probing via external SYSTEM entity URLs resolved by the parser; (c) denial of service via entity expansion (billion laughs). It also nullifies the parser's advertised DISALLOW_DOCTYPE_DECL/CUSTOM_XML_READER protections for tuple results.
candidates.prerequisites: Tuple results are parsed as SPARQL/XML (the format the client advertises/accepts for application/sparql-results+xml), and the JAXP XMLReader used by XMLReaderFactory does not externally restrict DTD/external entities (the default for standard Java 8 JAXP: DOCTYPE and external general entities are processed unless features/properties are set; this repository never sets them on this path). For the federation variant, SERVICE evaluation must be enabled and reachable from the query engine (the default resolver here is SPARQLServiceResolver). Applications that explicitly set XMLParserSettings.CUSTOM_XML_READER or DISALLOW_DOCTYPE_DECL still get the unhardened reader for tuple parsing.
candidates.root_cause: AbstractSPARQLXMLParser.parseQueryResultInternal() protects only the boolean-result branch: that branch honors XMLParserSettings.CUSTOM_XML_READER and applies every getCompulsoryXmlFeatureSettings() entry (SECURE_PROCESSING, DISALLOW_DOCTYPE_DECL, EXTERNAL_GENERAL_ENTITIES=false, EXTERNAL_PARAMETER_ENTITIES=false). The tuple-result branch instead calls XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader() and only sets an error handler, so JAXP defaults are used and DOCTYPE declarations/external entities are resolved. XMLReaderFactory itself sets only setNamespaceAware(true) and no entity/DTD restriction. The tuple format parser (SPARQLResultsXMLParser) always takes this branch, so even a caller that configures DISALLOW_DOCTYPE_DECL/CUSTOM_XML_READER is silently unprotected for tuple results.
candidates.title: SPARQL/XML tuple query results parsed with unhardened XMLReader (XXE)
candidates.trace: SPARQLProtocolSession.getBackgroundTupleQueryResult / getTupleQueryResult (http/client/.../SPARQLProtocolSession.java:722-728 and 758-766) -> QueryResultIO.createTupleParser(format, vf) (queryresultio/api/.../QueryResultIO.java:148-176) -> SPARQLResultsXMLParser.parseQueryResult -> parseQueryResultInternal(in, false, true) (SPARQLResultsXMLParser.java:70-84) -> tuple branch line 203 new XMLReader via XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader(), no features set (AbstractSPARQLXMLParser.java:201-211) -> SimpleSAXParser.parse(inputSource) -> default SAX entity resolution -> SPARQLResultsSAXParser converts element text (including entity-expanded content) into Literal/BNode/IRI values (SPARQLResultsSAXParser.java:109-139). Federation variant: RepositoryFederatedService.select prepares a TupleQuery on the SPARQLRepository built for the attacker's service URL (RepositoryFederatedService.java:127-152; SPARQLServiceResolver.java:92-97) and returns those bindings to the caller.
candidates.unverified: No runtime confirmation and no exploit payload were produced. The exact upstream fix/CVE identity for this snapshot was not verified (no network/history access), and the server-side federation chain assumes an RDF4J Server-like host using these libraries, since the server/workbench modules are not part of this snapshot. Line ranges refer to the source as assigned.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: Per get_source_scope: 1161 model-visible files, 0 excluded over 5 MiB, 0 excluded by sensitive-name/path filters, 0 symlinks excluded; binary-like files are refused/skipped by the read/search tools. The snapshot is the RDF4J 2.5-SNAPSHOT client-libraries aggregate (util, model, rio, queryresultio, query, queryalgebra-model, queryparser, queryrender, repository, http, sparqlbuilder, plus poms); test sources and build outputs are absent. I inspected the XML/JSON/RDF/query-result parsers, HTTP client/protocol, repository clients and federation, repository manager, and utility IO/file code, and searched for process execution, deserialization, class loading, URL opening, path handling, and XML parser configuration. Coverage is source-reading based; not every one of the 1161 files was read line-by-line.

Test sources and the http/server, sail, tools, workbench modules are not present, so any server-side or federated-deployment trace is a code-level inference rather than an end-to-end confirmed path.

rejected_leads.reason: Same missing-hardening pattern, but within this snapshot TransactionReader has no callers; its realistic attack surface is the RDF4J Server module, which is not included, so reachability could not be traced in the assigned tree.

rejected_leads.lead: JSON-LD remote @context/document loading during parse (rio/jsonld/JSONLDParser.java:97-106 uses default JsonLdOptions/jsonld-java DocumentLoader; JSONLDSettings in this snapshot has no secure-mode or document-loader restriction).
rejected_leads.reason: Remote context resolution is spec-driven behavior and no in-tree attacker-controlled call path or file:-scheme handling could be demonstrated; impact (SSRF) is plausible but weaker and less clearly a defect than the candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Binary tuple-result parser trusts length/count fields: readStringV2 allocates from a stream-provided int (queryresultio/binary/.../BinaryQueryResultParser.java:327-341), processNamespace grows an array from namespaceID (231-245), and the format-version check uses && instead of || (119).
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable with a malicious endpoint but impact is limited to resource exhaustion/DoS and runtime exceptions; lower severity than the XXE candidate, and no read/write primitive shown.

summary: Reviewed the assigned RDF4J 2.5-SNAPSHOT client-libraries snapshot (1161 model-visible source files; source filters as reported by get_source_scope: 0 files excluded for size/name/symlink, binary-like files skipped by the reader). The tree is the "client" aggregate (util, model, rio, queryresultio, query, queryalgebra-model, queryparser, queryrender, repository, http, sparqlbuilder; test sources stripped). I traced parser/IO/HTTP trust boundaries and found one strongest candidate: the SPARQL/XML tuple-result parse path builds an XMLReader with no DTD/external-entity hardening, even though the same class defines those restrictions as compulsory and applies them on the boolean-result path. A remote SPARQL endpoint (including one reached through the in-tree federation code, or an endpoint parsing untrusted results) can therefore inject a DOCTYPE/external entity that is expanded during tuple-result parsing, yielding local-file disclosure, SSRF, or entity-expansion DoS. No runtime testing was performed; this is a source-evidence lead.
